paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD's people don't have to trust in their own stuff. In Micah 5:10-11, the LORD says, "I will remove your horses from among you and wreck your chariots," and "I will remove the cities of your land and tear down all your strongholds." Horses, walls, and fortune-tellers are the things people lean on when they're nervous. The LORD says He'll take them away, so His people can lean on Him (Micah 5:10-12).

Then the LORD gets to the heart of it. He says He'll cut off the carved images and sacred pillars "so that you will no longer bow down to the work of your own hands" (Micah 5:13). Think about that for a second. I stamp cookies with my own handle, and I would NEVER bow down to a cookie! But people do it with things they've made, and the LORD says He'll end that. He wants His people's worship pointed at the One who made them, not at something they made.

And look at what the remnant of Jacob gets to be. Micah 5:7 says they're "like dew from the LORD," which doesn't "wait for man." Micah 5:8 says they're like a lion among the beasts of the forest. Both pictures show that their strength comes from the LORD, not from horses or walls. So here's the question for you, baker: what are YOUR chariots? Whatever it is, you can set it down and let the LORD be your strength. And the passage says the LORD will deal with the nations that have not obeyed Him (Micah 5:15), so you can trust Him to handle that part too.
